title: Negation-class parallel Pollard rho on P-256 with a global work meter and an exact report store priced by an executed AArch64 field listing (walk of 5fa78d62)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production P-256 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (negation-class parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=2048 adding walk on classes {P,-P} keyed by x, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes appended as 104-byte records to 2^16 append-only logs at the position the report's arrival index gives, duplicates recovered by an exact radix sort of each log on the full 256-bit key plus a k-way merge comparing full keys, re-walk solving), the walk of submission 5fa78d62-1c6b-46b8-b9cf-02481a49e645 (itself adapted from the class walk of submission 1c600df4), halts on every run after at most 2^127.72 units of C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions because a global work meter charges every action before it runs; all P-256 arithmetic is charged through the instruction counts of an executed AArch64 listing (field_listing.md, run by experiment.py Part C: Montgomery multiplication M=139, modular addition 20 and subtraction 19 charged A=20, inversion charged I=2^17 against 53,098 executed), giving 1,086 instructions and 1.086 units per step. The report store places no record at an address derived from its key: there is no slot index, no probe sequence, no replacement rule and no load factor, the occupancy of every log is fixed by the report count alone, and equal full keys are the only thing that can be reported as a collision. It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random mapping on N=(r-1)/2 classes with Brent-Pollard correction and a 5% slowdown allowance; index and distinguished bits pseudo-random; non-fruitless returns at most L_max^2/(2N)): H1 gives 0.395 at the S_ops budget, the phase-1 operation counter counts doublings so the arrivals reached are at least S_ops - 2^115.58 and H1 at that count gives 0.394851, and the failure rows (the Markov early-halt 0.002239 plus a tail below 3.8e-8) leave 0.392611, supported by toy runs that build, sort and merge the declared store. Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^60 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production P-256 checks of every identity the walk uses; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (T_c census, pipeline success with the declared record store built and sorted, long-trail trap test); Part C: executes the AArch64 field listing on production P-256 elements and points (kernel correctness, flag rule, inversion chain, batched additions and doublings) and recomputes the work ledger and the store ledger from the executed counts.
